why: The margin here is NARROW and the honest reading is that this is a commodity space where ours wins on one non-commodity property: the source of truth is a file this repository's own oracles already read, and the projector refuses rather than guesses when the source and the board disagree. Every alternative found either (a) makes GitHub the source of truth and syncs a local mirror down from it (gh-issue-sync, backlog.md, agilemarkdown), which inverts the direction this repo needs and puts the backlog behind a network call that CLAUDE.md records as the class of check that fails open, or (b) projects up but only creates, never reconciles field values (recurring-backlog-item-creator, the project-fields Action), or (c) is an IaC provider with no ProjectV2 field resource at all (terraform-provider-github / Pulumi github). The closest real competitor is gh-pm, a Go gh extension with a .gh-pm.yml holding exactly the field-alias mapping FIELD_MAP holds and with a documented --dry-run; if it also reconciled, this record would say adopt. What it does not do, on the evidence read, is plan a per-item diff of current-versus-desired field values and report a value it cannot resolve. That last behaviour is the whole point here: the defect this component was written to fix is a Lane option set retired by ADR-0016, and a projector that guessed `B harness` onto the nearest surviving option would have written 26 items into the RESUME lane. resolve_option returns None instead, and the live dry run reported 26 UNRESOLVED rather than 26 wrong writes. Second property, and it is a correction to the published record rather than a feature: the community's documented workaround for updateProjectV2Field clearing item values (discussion 198803, June 2026: 'retrieve existing options first, then include all of them') is INCOMPLETE. Measured here 2026-07-31 on a disposable field, passing the same option NAMES without their ids still regenerates the ids and clears every item value; only passing the existing `id` preserves them. Nothing found says this. It is why the Lane retype landed with zero data loss.

alternatives.name: gh-pm (github.com/yahsan2/gh-pm, Go, MIT)
alternatives.covers: the closest fit by a wide margin and the strongest candidate. A gh CLI extension purpose-built for Projects v2 plus Issues, with a `.gh-pm.yml` that carries a project reference and a field-alias mapping (`p0: "P0"`), which is structurally the same thing as FIELD_MAP plus resolve_option. It has a documented dry-run mode ('preview changes before applying them', --dry-run and --list), batch issue creation from a file (--from-file issues.yml), sub-issue duplicate detection, and it can set project field values and filter by them. It caches project metadata at init for speed, which is a thing ours does not do.
alternatives.gap: the config's field mapping reads as one-way input aliasing for CLI arguments, not a per-item desired-state reconciliation: no evidence found of a plan that classifies each (item, field) pair as set / skip / unresolved / missing-field, which is what makes the run idempotent and what makes a retired option value fail loudly. Its own README does not claim general idempotency; duplicate detection is scoped to sub-issues. It is also a Go binary and a gh extension install, added to a repository whose entire tools/ tree is stdlib Python that CI runs directly, and the backlog source would have to move from state/github-backlog-*.json into .gh-pm.yml, away from the file tests/test_ghpub_backlog.py currently asserts against.
alternatives.cost: gh extension install plus a Go binary on Windows, plus rewriting the 26-epic JSON into its YAML schema, plus losing the pure-Python planner that the tests exercise with no network.
alternatives.maturity: 6 stars, MIT, Go, README fetched 2026-07-31. Latest release date and commit activity NOT verified. Six stars is a real risk for a tool that would own the backlog projection.

alternatives.name: gh-issue-sync (github.com/mitsuhiko/gh-issue-sync)
alternatives.covers: the local-file-plus-GitHub problem, well: mirrors issues into a local .issues/ directory as Markdown with YAML front matter, allows local editing, and syncs changes back. That is a real answer to 'the backlog should be readable offline and diffable in a PR'.
alternatives.gap: the direction is wrong for this repository. It MIRRORS from GitHub, so GitHub is the source of truth and the local tree is a cache; here the JSON is the source and GitHub is the projection, which is the position tools/ghpub/publish_backlog.py's docstring has taken since it was written. It also works on issues, not on Projects v2 custom field values, which is where both measured defects lived. Nothing found suggests it touches a project board at all.
alternatives.cost: not applicable, it does not cover the field-sync requirement.
alternatives.maturity: found via search 2026-07-31; language, licence, release activity NOT verified.

alternatives.name: Project Fields Action (github.com/marketplace/actions/project-fields)
alternatives.covers: reading and writing a project item's field values from inside a GitHub Actions workflow, which is the natural home for 'when an issue is labelled X, set field Y'. Zero local install, runs where the token already is.
alternatives.gap: it is an event-driven mutator, not a regenerator. There is no source file it reconciles against, so it cannot answer 'does the board match the backlog', and it cannot run in a dry run on the operator's machine before anything is written. Adopting it also means a workflow with a project-scoped token, and it would still need a declarative source for the desired values, which is the part this component actually is.
alternatives.cost: a workflow file plus a PAT with project scope stored as a secret, in a repo where CLAUDE.md already flags network-dependent checks as failing open.
alternatives.maturity: listed on the Actions Marketplace 2026-07-31; version, author and maintenance NOT verified.

alternatives.name: recurring-backlog-item-creator (github.com/Rindrics/recurring-backlog-item-creator)
alternatives.covers: the exact top-level shape: a YAML configuration file that automatically creates and manages GitHub issues in a project backlog. Closest thing found to 'declarative source, GitHub projection' in the create direction.
alternatives.gap: scoped to RECURRING items, which is a scheduling concern this backlog does not have (26 one-off epics, none repeating). No evidence found that it writes ProjectV2 custom field values, and the search result explicitly did not establish its duplicate-prevention mechanism, which is the property this component's title-keyed idempotency depends on.
alternatives.cost: unknown; not evaluated further once the recurring scope was clear.
alternatives.maturity: NOT verified beyond the repository existing.

alternatives.name: backlog.md (self.md/tools/backlog-md) and agilemarkdown (github.com/mreider/agilemarkdown)
alternatives.covers: the philosophy directly, and both are better at the local half than ours: every task is a Markdown file with YAML metadata in a backlog/ directory inside the git repo, so the board IS the repository, versioned and diffable. agilemarkdown's `am sync` regenerates derived views and validates each item against a JSON Schema, which is a validation layer this component does not have.
alternatives.gap: both replace GitHub Projects rather than project onto it. Their board is rendered from the Markdown; they do not write ProjectV2 field values, so neither addresses the actual defect. Adopting either is a decision to abandon Zion, which is a legitimate option and is argued in docs/specs/2026-07-31-project-federation.md section 6, but it is not a substitute for this component, it is a substitute for the board.
alternatives.cost: a new CLI plus a backlog/ tree, and the loss of GitHub's issue cross-references and notifications.
alternatives.maturity: both actively written about in 2026 (self.md and thedavestack.com posts found this session). Releases, licences and star counts NOT verified.

alternatives.name: terraform-provider-github / Pulumi github provider (v6.13.1, 2026-04-29)
alternatives.covers: the general 'declarative desired state, plan before apply, converge' pattern properly, with a real diff engine, state file, and a mature plan/apply loop that is strictly better engineering than a hand-rolled planner.
alternatives.gap: no ProjectV2 resource found. The Pulumi package is generated from the Terraform GitHub provider, and neither registry page surfaced a github_project_v2 or a project field resource; the provider's project resources are the classic (v1) projects, which are a different API. Terraform would also introduce a state file as a second source of truth about the board, which is exactly the duplication docs/specs/2026-07-31-project-federation.md section 1.3 measures going wrong between two boards over one repo.
alternatives.cost: a Terraform or Pulumi toolchain plus state storage plus a token, for a resource type that appears not to exist.
alternatives.maturity: Pulumi github provider v6.13.1 published 2026-04-29 per the registry page. Whether any version exposes ProjectV2 fields was NOT verified against the provider's resource index, only against search results, so this gap is the least certain claim in this record.

alternatives.name: plain `gh project item-edit` in a shell script
alternatives.covers: the simplest correct option, and it must be named because this repo's own rules require it. gh 2.92.0 supports --field-id, --single-select-option-id, --date, --number and --text, so a 20-line bash loop over the JSON would write the same values this component writes.
alternatives.gap: it cannot do the two things that matter. It has no way to know an option name maps to an option id without a lookup, so the script hardcodes ids that change whenever a field is recreated; and it has no current-value comparison, so every run rewrites every value and a failure mid-run is indistinguishable from success. cli/cli issue 7962 also records that item-edit cannot CLEAR a value, so a shell approach has no way to unset a field that should no longer be set. The planner is 48 lines and is the part under test; the gh calls around it are the thin shell a script would be all of.
alternatives.cost: zero install, and it is what the repository would have had if this had not been written. Roughly 20 lines against 373.
alternatives.maturity: gh project is generally available (github.blog announcement) and is already a dependency here.

evidence: Read tools/ghpub/publish_backlog.py in full, 373 lines, the only .py in the directory. Read tests/test_ghpub_backlog.py in full, 21 tests. Read docs/prior-art/tools-snapshot.json as the depth template. Ran, read-only: `gh project field-list 3 --owner ShovalBenjer --format json` (20 fields), `gh project item-list 3 --owner ShovalBenjer --limit 100 --format json` (26 items), the same pair for project 4 (29 items) and for solosolve-ai project 1 (30 items), and `gh repo list ShovalBenjer --limit 50 --json name,visibility`. Ran, write, on a DISPOSABLE field created and deleted for the purpose (`ZZ probe`, PVTSSF_lAHOBTKVvM4At4WJzhZTJ9w): field-create, item-edit to set a value, updateProjectV2Field WITHOUT option ids (ids regenerated 3a2f5fc8 to f93e7b59, item value read back as null), item-edit to re-set, updateProjectV2Field WITH the existing option id (ids unchanged, item value read back as 'Z renamed'), field-delete. Introspected ProjectV2SingleSelectFieldOptionInput and confirmed it accepts id, name, color, description. Ran the publisher itself: `--fields` dry run against the live board (130 planned rows, 26 unresolved on the retired Lane letters, 26 no-field before Evidence state existed), then `--fields --execute` twice (set=26 skip=104, then skip=130). Searches run 2026-07-31: GitHub Projects v2 as code declarative sync; gh CLI extension setting field values idempotently; terraform/pulumi ProjectV2 field resources; backlog-as-code markdown-to-issues generators. Pages fetched: github.com/yahsan2/gh-pm (config shape, dry-run, MIT, Go, 6 stars) and github.com/orgs/community/discussions/198803 (June 2026, confirms updateProjectV2Field is a full replacement that clears item values; its stated workaround is to re-send all existing options, which my measurement shows is insufficient without ids). NOT VERIFIED: I installed and ran none of the alternatives, so every migration cost is an estimate from reading. I did not verify gh-pm's release cadence or whether a newer version added reconciliation. I did not enumerate the Terraform GitHub provider's resource index directly, so 'no ProjectV2 resource' rests on search results rather than on the provider docs. I did not test whether updateProjectV2Field preserves values when adding a NEW option alongside id-carrying existing ones, which is the case the operator will hit next.
recheck: Run `python -m pytest tests/test_ghpub_backlog.py -q` (must stay green before any migration is discussed), then `gh release list --repo yahsan2/gh-pm --limit 5` and `gh api repos/yahsan2/gh-pm --jq '.pushed_at, .stargazers_count'`, and check the Terraform GitHub provider resource index for any projectv2 field resource. Then WebSearch 'gh-pm reconcile desired state project field values dry-run diff' and 'updateProjectV2Field add option preserve existing item values id'. RE-OPEN THIS VERDICT IF any of: (a) gh-pm documents a per-item desired-state diff with an unresolved-value failure mode, in which case adopt it and delete the planner, (b) the Terraform or Pulumi GitHub provider ships a ProjectV2 field-value resource, in which case the plan/apply engine is strictly better than a hand-rolled one, (c) GitHub ships a documented partial-update mutation for single-select options, which would make the id-preservation finding in this record obsolete, or (d) the operator closes Zion per docs/specs/2026-07-31-project-federation.md section 6, in which case this component has no board to project onto and should be deleted rather than defended.
what_ours_does: One file, publish_backlog.py, 387 lines, stdlib only plus the gh binary, dry run by default. It reads state/github-backlog-*.json and projects it onto a repository's labels, milestones and issues (idempotent by TITLE, not id, deliberately: renaming an epic creates a new issue rather than silently mutating one, which keeps the audit trail on GitHub's side), then optionally adds each issue to a Projects v2 board and, new on 2026-07-31, reconciles the board's custom field values. build_body renders the epic header, grounding paragraph and task checklist, rendering a task prefixed DONE as checked so a republish shows real progress. FIELD_MAP declares the five fields the JSON owns (Priority, Ingestion, Lane, Autonomy, Evidence state); Status and anything that is a reaction to work happening are deliberately absent and stay hand-set, because one writer per field is the property that makes drift detectable. item_key encodes a measured gh quirk: item-list lowercases only the FIRST character of a field name ('ZZ probe' becomes 'zZ probe'), so a .lower() comparison reads None forever and rewrites on every run. resolve_option maps a JSON value to exactly one option by exact name, then leading token ('S2' finds 'S2 45min', 'A' finds 'A harness'), then case-insensitive prefix, returning nothing on ambiguity or on a value the board cannot represent. plan_field_writes is pure and is the oracle: it takes epics, fields and items and returns one row per pair with an action of set, skip, no-field, no-item or unresolved, so nothing is dropped silently and the whole decision layer is testable with no network and no token. sync_project_fields is the thin gh shell around it, printing the plan on a dry run rather than refusing to run, and exit_code_for turns the plan's outcome counts into a process exit status so the dry run is wirable as a drift detector.
strongest_counterargument: This component exists to keep a surface honest that nobody reads. The two defects it was written to fix (a Lane option set retired for one day, an Evidence field holding one identical string across 23 of 26 items) both survived because the board is written and read by the same one person, and a third defect the brief did not name is still live: Autonomy reads the same value on 26 of 26 items, so the field the companion spec calls the most valuable on the board has never demonstrated it can take a second value. Fixing the rot mechanism does not answer whether the surface was worth having, and docs/specs/2026-07-31-project-federation.md section 6 argues at length that it was not. If that argument wins, the correct action is `gh project close 3` and deleting this file, and this record's keep-ours verdict evaporates with the board. The second cut is that the defended margin over gh-pm is one behaviour, the unresolved row, and gh-pm is 6 stars of Go that could add it in an afternoon. The third is scope: 387 lines now do labels, milestones, issue bodies, project membership and field reconciliation in one flat main(), and the field-sync half shares nothing with the issue half except the JSON it reads. Two files would be the honest shape, and the only reason it is one is that this component is exactly at the 300-line threshold where the repo demands this record, so splitting it would make the requirement disappear rather than be met. Finally, the reconciliation is a detector and not an oracle: `--fields` exits 1 when the board cannot be made to match the source, but nothing in tools/gate/ or in CI calls it, so the signal exists and no oracle reads it, and until something does this is Option B with an undocumented manual annex plus a better story, which is precisely what the companion spec warned a hybrid becomes when its seam is unchecked.
